topic: Safe and Efficient String Substring Extraction
explanation: In C++, extracting substrings from strings is a common operation, especially when dealing with iterators in containers or objects that return strings. The concept focuses on using std::string::substr to safely retrieve a portion of a string, as seen in scenarios like processing file paths or data streams. Best practices include checking string lengths to avoid inefficiencies, understanding that substr creates a new string (which can lead to unnecessary copies), and preferring std::string_view (in C++17+) for read-only access to avoid copies. Common pitfalls include assuming the string is long enough, which substr handles gracefully by returning the available substring without exceptions, and chaining method calls without error handling. In real-world usage, this technique is essential for tasks like truncating log messages or extracting prefixes/suffixes in data processing loops.
